correctness.rationale: For a fixed n>=3, all 16^n independent edge truth-table choices are counted exactly. Boolean product has a diagonal one iff the cyclic constraints have a solution. Seven row/column-swap orbits cover all sixteen relations, and the displayed integer T counts uniform multipliers in all orbit representatives. The acceptance vector g has entries 16-2^(4-w), since each allowed pair forbids a distinct B entry for a zero product diagonal. Integer multiplication verifies (T-4I)(T-2I)(T^2-17T+48I)g=0, and the first four counts 12,175,2397,32377 determine the recurrence uniquely. Hence the all-n formula follows. Independent exhaustive counts and inclusion-exclusion for n=3,4 agree. No finite computation is substituted for the polynomial annihilator argument.

value.rationale: This resolves the explicit all-cycle Conjecture 20 of Horak and Semaev (2026) in its exact intended model by supplying a corrected formula for every cycle size, not merely a finite counterexample. The discrepancy is quantified for every n and supported by a compact explicit seven-orbit transition calculation. Exact finite-domain CSP consistency counts are natural invariants connected to sparse polynomial-solving statistics; 60 of 4096 systems change classification at n=3, so even the first numerical boundary is substantively distinct. The exponential correction is lower order asymptotically but decisive for an exact enumerative conjecture.
